checked_contracts: TSetup<false> custom-factory construction, BuildGraph reset behavior and graph invalidation agree with the referenced public test APIs.
The generated factory resolves the linked production WrapKqpRangeMinMax callable rather than embedding a substitute implementation.
The source fixture, witness counters and captured factory state outlive every computation node and graph that references them.
The optional Int64 full-scan oracle and null-key frame membership match the collector boundary conventions for admitted finite and suffix frames.
Mixed mode constructs the real WinFramesCollector and WinFrame APIs; the collector cleans retained rows on Finish, supporting the zero-live-row expectation.
Repeated input yields, repeated Finish, cancellation before the first result, early cancellation after results and four reset cycles have separate generated cases.
Allocator limits are installed after input row construction but before production queue growth; trigger positions target capacities two, four and thirty-two.
The allocator increase-limit callback and limits are removed before cleanup; failed reserve accounting is checked independently from successful allocations.
Lifetime peak growth and sampled runtime usage are recorded as separate metrics with an explicit prepared-graph baseline.
Generated source remains in process memory, and this review stores only approved metadata, source hashes and verdicts.

limitations: Int64 payloads only; SQL typed coverage is separate.
Source fetch/allocation counters are measured, internal deque comparisons are not instrumented.
Allocator-limit rejection covers reserve accounting before allocation; std::vector allocation-failure injection is not included.
Public allocator metrics are process-local MiniKQL accounting, not RSS.
Peak deltas measure growth above the allocator prior high-water mark; sampled_used_delta measures observed runtime usage above its prepared-graph baseline. Neither is a query RSS bound.
Mixed mode uses the real collector and frame length; full RBO lowering and other native functions remain SQL acceptance responsibilities.
GetUsed modulo-page cleanup check assumes no unrelated offloaded allocations enter the fixture; native validation is still required.
